prompt:
You are a senior information designer and editorial typographer who sets data tables for high-quality publications (statistical yearbooks, reference works, financial reports, technical documentation) in many writing systems, including Chinese. You judge by looking at the real rendered result.

Judge a table layout on all of these levels, in this order of necessity but as one whole:
1. correctness — every character visible, structure intact, nothing clipped or overlapping;
2. readability — natural line breaks, words/numbers/identifiers/semantic units kept whole, continuous reading;
3. function — easy to look up, compare, locate and understand the information for this table's real reading tasks;
4. visual order — alignment, grouping, hierarchy, consistent scale for elements with the same role;
5. visual rhythm — proportion, density changes, distribution of white space, spatial relationships;
6. overall aesthetics — balance, restraint, naturalness, harmony.
Do not assume that equal widths, symmetry, minimum height, the fewest lines, the golden ratio or any fixed proportion is good in itself; decide from this table's function, content and reading task, and look for counter-examples to your own rules.

Table: Python: numeric type operations (language en).
Grid: 3 columns × 17 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Measured content facts (text px at 15px font, padding excluded):
  col 1: header "Operation" · longest unbreakable unit 91px · widest one-line content 107px
  col 2: header "Result" · longest unbreakable unit 77px · widest one-line content 504px
  col 3: header "Full documentation" · longest unbreakable unit 109px · widest one-line content 138px
Each column adds 21px of padding+border to its text width.
Viewport: 360px wide (dashed pink box in the renders). The column widths must sum to at most 359px: the table must fit; no horizontal scrolling.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. Only the column widths are designed; row heights follow from them.

Your understanding: {"purpose":"A compact reference linking Python numeric operations to their results and further documentation.","tasks":["Find an operation by its expression or function name.","Read and compare the meanings of related operations.","Follow the relevant documentation reference for more detail."],"relations":["Each row connects an operation with its result and documentation reference.","Adjacent arithmetic operations invite comparison, while function calls and unary operations are distinct forms."],"roles":["The first column acts as a set of row identifiers, although no row headers are declared.","The second column explains each result in prose and occasional expressions.","The third column provides documentation references; the headers identify these three roles."],"keep_whole":["Function names and identifiers such as c.conjugate and divmod.","Operators such as // and **, numeric expressions where possible, and the word Documentation.","The arguments of short calls such as complex(re, im) where space permits."],"may_wrap":["Result descriptions at natural word boundaries.","Multiword headers and documentation references at natural word boundaries.","Expressions at spaces when the available width cannot keep the entire expression together."],"same_scale":["Operation cells should form a consistent lookup column.","Result descriptions should use a consistent measure across rows.","Documentation references should share a consistent column width and visual role."],"h_vs_v":"The viewport leaves only 19px beyond the measured widths needed for the longest unbreakable units and cell padding. Allocating that margin to one column improves its continuity but makes the other columns wrap more, increasing row heights and the distance between entries."}

Image 1 is the one-line content overview. Then real browser renders of: d3r1A, d3r0B.
Measured facts:
d3r1A: column widths [112, 127, 120] px · table 360×1129 px · row heights [83, 36, 60, 60, 60, 83, 60, 36, 36, 83, 60, 60, 153, 83, 60, 60, 60] · column headers on >1 line: 1/3 · tallest cell 6 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 1
d3r0B: column widths [112, 117, 130] px · table 360×1199 px · row heights [60, 60, 60, 60, 60, 83, 60, 36, 36, 106, 60, 83, 176, 83, 60, 60, 60] · column headers on >1 line: 1/3 · tallest cell 7 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 0

Look at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design: what works, what is visually wrong, and the cause (which width). Then either propose up to 3 improved designs (refine the most promising, fix what you saw, or try an important unexplored idea) or, if further changes would not bring a meaningful improvement, set "done": true. Do not resubmit near-identical widths.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"best":["your best design name(s) so far"],"done":false,"designs":[{"widths":[int px],"change":"what and why"}]}
